keywords: works in repo fails when packaged
title: Moved config into a new directory beside the code but never added it to the ship manifest — checks passed in place and failed everywhere else
summary: A new preset directory was added beside the source tree but never added to the manifest listing which paths get copied and shipped. Checks passed when run in place and collapsed against a copied tree — the same gap that ships a package missing its data files.
mistake: While extending a feature, code went into the existing source directory but its configuration was factored out into a brand-new sibling directory. The list at the top of the acceptance script naming which paths belong to the deliverable was never updated. Run normally, from the repository root, every check passed and the suite reported a clean result, because the new directory was physically present. The suite's self-validation mode, which copies only the manifested paths into a scratch directory and re-runs each check there, then failed two checks with a file-not-found error while the normal run stayed green. Without that second mode the release would have been declared complete and the artifact would have broken on the first machine that received it. The identical gap exists in a container build file's copy instructions, a Python package-data or manifest template, a Node package file allowlist, and a CI artifact upload path.
instead: The moment configuration, assets, presets, fixtures, or templates are placed in a directory that did not exist before, update every place that enumerates the shipped tree in the same change. Find them with a single search across the repository for the manifest keywords used by your ecosystem: the acceptance script's path list, MANIFEST templates, package-data declarations, container copy instructions, package file allowlists, and CI upload globs. Then, when the check suite has a mode that re-runs itself against a copy or a fresh install, never accept the in-place run as proof of completion: run both, and treat completion as reached only when both are green. On any change that introduces a new top-level directory, run the copied-tree mode first, since it is the fastest way to surface the omission.
